newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street stocks steady, eyes on bonds, FOMC.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street stocks steady, eyes on bonds, FOMC.

text.p: Wall Street stocks were steady and nearly flat, watching the bond market, as Federal Reserve policy makers wrapped up a two-day meeting which was not expected to change interest rates.
Stocks focused on interest rates, individual issues and a key employment report due on Thursday, largely ignoring a slight dip in U.S. factory orders for May, analysts said.
Factory orders declined 0.7 percent in May compared with a forecast 0.2 percent decline and an upwardly-revised 1.4 percent increase in April.

"Factory orders, which include orders to both durable goods manufacturers and non-durable goods manufacturers, are usually old news," Pierre Ellis, senior economist at Primark Decision Economics. "The situation remains that orders paused a bit in the second quarter after the first quarter."
The stock market was quiet ahead of a Federal Reserve announcement, expected at 1415 EDT/1815 GMT, analysts said.

"The market is trading kind of flat," Henry Herrmann, chief investment officer at Waddell & Read, said. "It's looking at the bond market, which is looking at the employment report tomorrow, and at the remote chance of Fed action."
The Dow Jones Industrial Average, which finished stronger yesterday, drifted between minute gains and losses.
It was down around three points at 7719 while the long bond was up 7/32 at a 6.73 percent yield.
The Nasdaq composite was up around three points at 1441.
